newsitem.title: CHINA: LCH Bank to develop credit card services.
newsitem.headline: LCH Bank to develop credit card services.

text.p: Liu Chong Hing Bank Ltd said on Tuesday it planned to invest about HK$10 million to develop its credit card business.

"We are going to invest HK$10 million to develop our credit business. We aim at providing the services to our existing customers," said the bank's executive director L.Y. Nam at a press briefing on Tuesday.
Nam said the bank had earlier this year opened a branch in Macau and the bank planned to open more branches in Zhuhai and Zhong Shan in China.

Liu Chong Hing Bank also plans to expand into the China market through the relationship with COSCO Pacific Ltd in the mainland after COSCO agreed in July to take a 20 percent of stake in the bank, Nam said.
"One of our goals is through COSCO to expand our services in China," Nam said.

"COSCO is a big Chinese firm, they have offices in many provinces and cities in China, through its relationship, we believe that we can benefit if COSCO introduces its customers to our bank," he said.

Liu Chong Bank had earlier on Tuesday reported a 26.31 percent rise in profit to HK$341.26 million for the six months to June 30, mainly boosted by a 25.04 percent increase in net interest income to HK$499.83 million during the period.
Nam said the recent high interbank rate was expected to have a mild impact to the interest margin of Liu Chong Hing Bank.
"Our bank's capital is relatively high and many of the loans are from our capital or shareholders fund," Nam said.

"If the interbank rate stays at the current high level for not more than the next three weeks to a month, we do not expect any significant impact (to the bank interest margin)," Nam said. "If the interbank rates stay at the high level for a much longer period of time, I think the prime rate will be increased and that the interest margin will be narrowed," Nam added.
Liu Chong Hing Bank said its interest margin was at 3.46 percent, compared with 3.6 percent for the first half of 1996 and 3.39 percent for the whole of 1996.
"We expect (local) interest rates will go up steadily in the second half, tracking the U.S interest rates," Nam added.
